basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 6.' and it opens '| Vers. 6. Sed fons ascendens e terra universam ejus superficiem irrigabat. Fons autem'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 6. Sed fons ascendens e terra universam ejus superficiem irrigabat. Fons autem ille, vel per occultos meatus terrae decurrens ascendebat ad irrigandam terrae superficiem, more Nili fluminis qui alvei sui metas progrediens irrigat plana Aegypti: vel etiam irrigans universam superficiem terrae, non quo omnem terrae superficiem operiret, sed rivatim more fluminum per diversa loca dirivaretur. Vel, quod melius placet more sacrae Scripturae, singularem posuit pro plurali, vel fontem pro fontibus, sicut muscam pro muscis, ranam pro ranis. Aut etiam fontem propter universitatem omnium aquarum quae simul sunt et quasi unus fons in matrice abysso.
